name: Jimi Hendrix
blurb: Redefined what an electric guitar could do with feedback, distortion and sheer volume. His sound is a direct ancestor of heavy metal guitar.

name: Led Zeppelin
blurb: Blueprint for hard rock and heavy metal: crushing riffs, thunderous drums and a mythic stage presence. They disbanded after drummer John Bonham's death in 1980.

name: The Stooges
blurb: Raw, abrasive proto-punk that prefigured both punk and the rawer edges of metal. Iggy Pop's confrontational stage act became a template.

name: Black Sabbath
blurb: Their dark, down-tuned, doom-laden sound is widely regarded as the birth of heavy metal. Almost every later metal subgenre traces back to Tony Iommi's riffs.

name: The Who
blurb: Pioneers of loud, aggressive power-chord rock and the guitar-smashing stage show. Their volume and rock-opera ambition shaped hard rock.

name: David Bowie
blurb: Glam-era shape-shifter whose Ziggy Stardust persona influenced the theatrical side of rock and metal. He also produced and championed the Stooges.

name: AC/DC
blurb: Stripped-down, blues-based hard rock built on Angus Young's riffs and showmanship. Back in Black is one of the best-selling albums ever made.

name: Judas Priest
blurb: Defined the leather-and-studs look and the twin-guitar sound of heavy metal. Their lean, fast approach shaped both NWOBHM and thrash.

name: Ramones
origin: Forest Hills, Queens, New York, USA
blurb: Fast, minimal, three-chord songs that kicked off punk rock. Their speed and brevity fed straight into thrash metal's DNA.

name: Motörhead
blurb: Lemmy's band fused punk speed and metal heaviness before the term crossover existed. A direct influence on thrash and speed metal.

name: Sex Pistols
blurb: Brought punk to the British mainstream with notoriety and one studio album. Their short-lived rebellion shook rock's establishment.

name: Van Halen
blurb: Eddie Van Halen's two-handed tapping and virtuosity raised the bar for rock and metal guitar. They made flashy technique a mainstream ideal.

name: Saxon
blurb: One of the bands most closely identified with the New Wave of British Heavy Metal. Their working-class anthems found a huge audience.

name: Iron Maiden
blurb: The flagship band of the NWOBHM, mixing galloping rhythms, twin-guitar harmonies and epic storytelling. One of metal's biggest touring acts.

name: Misfits
blurb: Horror-punk pioneers whose imagery and melodic hardcore influenced Metallica, Slayer and many others. Metallica later covered their songs.

name: Ozzy Osbourne
blurb: Sabbath's original singer rebuilt his career as a solo star, with Randy Rhoads' neo-classical playing at the front. A defining figure of 1980s metal.

name: Mötley Crüe
blurb: Leading band of the Sunset Strip glam-metal scene. Their image and platinum albums made hard rock a 1980s MTV staple.

name: Venom
blurb: Raw, Satanic-themed and deliberately extreme, they gave black metal its name. A huge influence on thrash, death and black metal.

name: Metallica
blurb: Took thrash from the underground to arenas. Their 1983-1988 run of albums defined the genre.

name: Slayer
blurb: The darkest and fastest of the Big Four. Reign in Blood set a benchmark for extreme metal.

name: Anthrax
blurb: Bridged thrash with humour and hardcore, and later crossed over with rap. Part of the Big Four.

name: Megadeth
blurb: Dave Mustaine's technical, aggressive answer to his old band. Part of the Big Four.

name: Exodus
blurb: Bay Area thrash pioneers and an incubator for Kirk Hammett. Bonded by Blood is a genre classic.

name: Death
blurb: Chuck Schuldiner's band is often called the founder of death metal and evolved toward progressive complexity.

name: S.O.D.
blurb: Stormtroopers of Death mixed thrash with hardcore and dark humour. Speak English or Die helped invent crossover.

name: Possessed
origin: San Francisco Bay Area, California, USA
blurb: Jeff Becerra's band helped give death metal its name and sound. Seven Churches is a foundational album.

name: Sepultura
blurb: Brazil's thrash and death metal giants brought extreme metal to a global audience.

name: The Exploited
blurb: Loud, aggressive Scottish punk that helped build the crossover between punk and metal.

name: Deep Purple
blurb: Alongside Sabbath and Zeppelin, one of the pioneers of hard rock and heavy metal, with Ritchie Blackmore's riffs and organ-driven power.

name: Hawkwind
blurb: Space-rock pioneers, and the band Lemmy played bass for before founding Motörhead.

name: Raven
blurb: Fast, high-energy NWOBHM band who toured with early Metallica and influenced American speed and thrash metal.

name: Diamond Head
blurb: NWOBHM band whose riffs deeply influenced Metallica, who covered several of their songs.

name: Discharge
blurb: Created the fast, relentless d-beat style that shaped crust, grindcore and thrash.

name: Mercyful Fate
blurb: King Diamond's falsetto and occult imagery, plus intricate twin-guitar writing, influenced thrash and black metal.

name: Overkill
blurb: East Coast thrash stalwarts with a long career built on relentless intensity.

name: Dark Angel
blurb: Technical, brutal thrash from California. Darkness Descends set a high bar for speed.

name: Testament
blurb: Bay Area thrash band, formed as Legacy, whose melodic leads and Chuck Billy's vocals kept them in the first rank.

name: Kreator
blurb: One of the German thrash trio. Pleasure to Kill helped lay foundations for death metal.

name: Celtic Frost
blurb: Evolved from Hellhammer into one of extreme metal's most innovative bands, pushing into avant-garde territory.

name: Bathory
blurb: Quorthon's one-man project is regarded as a forefather of black metal and later Viking metal.

name: Pantera
blurb: Reinvented themselves as a groove-heavy metal band with Cowboys from Hell and became 1990s metal's biggest act.
